clubfoot.name: Clubfoot (Talipes Equinovarus)
clubfoot.seo_title: Clubfoot Treatment Karachi | Best Pediatric Orthopedic Surgeon
clubfoot.seo_description: Specialized Clubfoot treatment in Karachi by Dr. Ayesha Saeed, Gold Medalist Pediatric Orthopedic Surgeon trained at SickKids Canada. Safe Ponseti Method.
clubfoot.intro: Clubfoot, or congenital talipes equinovarus, is a common birth defect where an infant's foot is twisted inward and downward. At birth, the tendons connecting the muscles to the bone are shorter than usual, causing the foot to hold this position. If left untreated, clubfoot does not improve and can cause severe walking disabilities as the child grows.
symptoms: The top of the foot is usually twisted downward and inward, increasing the arch and turning the heel inward.
The foot may be turned so severely that it actually looks as if it's upside down.
The calf muscles in the affected leg are typically underdeveloped.
The affected foot may be slightly shorter than the other foot, but it is not painful for the baby.
causes: Idiopathic: Most cases occur without a known cause in otherwise healthy babies.
Genetic Factor: A family history of clubfoot increases the risk of a child being born with it.
Neuromuscular conditions: In some cases, it can be associated with other skeletal abnormalities like spina bifida.
Environmental factor: Smoking during pregnancy significantly increases the risk.
clubfoot.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed specializes in the non-surgical correction of clubfoot using the internationally recognized **Ponseti Method**. This involves a series of gentle manual manipulations of the foot followed by the application of long-leg plaster casts, replaced weekly (usually 5 to 7 casts). After casting, a minor outpatient procedure called a tenotomy (numbing and clipping the Achilles tendon) is performed. The correction is then maintained using a specialized foot abduction brace (boots and bar) worn according to a strict schedule to prevent recurrence.

ddh.name: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (DDH)
ddh.seo_title: DDH Specialist Pakistan | Hip Dysplasia Treatment Karachi & Lahore
ddh.seo_description: Early detection and expert treatment of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (DDH) in Pakistan. Gold Medalist care from Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
ddh.intro: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip (DDH) is a condition where the ball-and-socket joint of the hip does not form properly in babies and young children. The socket is too shallow, meaning the ball (femoral head) can slip out easily or become completely dislocated. Early screening and intervention are vital to avoid long-term mobility issues, limp, or premature arthritis.
symptoms: Asymmetrical skin folds on the thigh or buttocks.
Decreased flexibility or range of motion in one hip compared to the other.
One leg appearing shorter than the other.
A clicking sound or 'clunk' when rotating the baby's hips during diaper changes.
Developing a limp or waddling gait once the child begins to walk.
causes: Breech presentation: Babies positioned bottom-first in the womb are at higher risk.
Family history: Having a parent or sibling with DDH increases the likelihood.
Firstborn status: The tight space of a first pregnancy can restrict fetal movement.
Tight swaddling: Traditional straight-leg swaddling can prevent normal hip development.
ddh.treatment: Treatment depends heavily on the child's age. For infants under 6 months, Dr. Ayesha Saeed utilizes the **Pavlik Harness**, a dynamic brace that holds the baby's hips in a bent, spread-apart position to naturally deepen the socket. For children diagnosed later (6 to 18 months), **closed reduction** (manipulating the joint under anesthesia) and application of a **Spica Cast** are preferred. Older children or complex cases may require **open reduction surgery** and pelvic osteotomies to reconstruct the hip joint.

bow-legs.name: Bow Legs (Genu Varum)
bow-legs.seo_title: Bow Legs Treatment Pakistan | Pediatric Knee Correction
bow-legs.seo_description: Is your child's leg bowing normal? Learn when to consult Dr. Ayesha Saeed, leading Pediatric Orthopedic Surgeon for Bow Legs treatment in Pakistan.
bow-legs.intro: Bow legs (genu varum) is a condition where a child's legs curve outward at the knees while the ankles touch. This is highly common and normal in infants and toddlers up to 18-24 months (physiological bowing). However, if the bowing persists beyond age 2, worsens, or affects only one leg, it may point to a pathological cause like Rickets or Blount's disease.
symptoms: A distinct gap between the knees when standing with ankles together.
An outward curvature of the shins and thighs.
Awkward walking gait (turning toes inward or waddling).
Knee or hip pain in older children and teenagers if bowing is untreated.
causes: Physiological Bowing: Natural development resulting from the baby's position in the womb.
Rickets: Bone softening due to Vitamin D, Calcium, or phosphate deficiency.
Blount's Disease: An abnormality in the growth plate at the top of the shinbone (tibia).
Infection or Trauma: Injuries affecting the inner growth plate of the knee joint.
bow-legs.treatment: Physiological bowing requires only regular observation and reassure parents that it will resolve naturally by age 2. Pathological bowing, such as that caused by Rickets, is corrected with dietary modifications and Vitamin D therapy. For conditions like Blount's disease or severe persistent deformities, Dr. Ayesha Saeed implements customized orthotic braces, serial casting, or modern minimally invasive procedures such as **Guided Growth** (using temporary small plates to straighten the leg as the child grows).

knock-knees.name: Knock Knees (Genu Valgum)
knock-knees.seo_title: Knock Knees Correction | Dr. Ayesha Saeed Pediatric Orthopedics
knock-knees.seo_description: Professional evaluation and correction for Knock Knees in children. Gold Medalist Orthopedic expert Dr. Ayesha Saeed offers compassionate care.
knock-knees.intro: Knock knees (genu valgum) is a condition where the knees tilt inward and touch each other when the child stands with the ankles apart. Like bow legs, mild knock knees are a normal part of development in most children between 3 and 5 years old. The alignment usually straightens by age 7 to 8. Assessment is required if the gap between ankles is large, asymmetrical, or accompanied by pain.
symptoms: Knees touch but ankles remain wide apart when standing.
An inward tilt of the legs and shins.
An unusual gait or frequent tripping while running.
Pain in the knees, hips, or feet, or difficulty keeping up with peers in sports.
causes: Developmental variation: Normal growth changes in young children.
Severe nutritional deficiency: Soft bones due to Vitamin D/Calcium deficiency.
Growth plate damage: Trauma or infection affecting the outer knee growth plate.
Obesity: Extra strain on growing joints can exacerbate structural alignment.
knock-knees.treatment: Most developmental cases require only monitoring. If the condition is pathological or severe in older children (over 10 years), surgical option is considered. Dr. Ayesha Saeed is highly skilled in **Guided Growth surgical technique (Hemi-epiphysiodesis)**, where a small plate is temporarily placed on the inner side of the knee growth plate to allow the outer side to grow and straighten the leg over 12-18 months. This minimally invasive method avoids major bone-cutting surgery.

flat-feet.name: Flat Feet (Pes Planus)
flat-feet.seo_title: Flat Feet Treatment | Pediatric Foot Arch Specialist Pakistan
flat-feet.seo_description: Does your child have flat feet? Learn about flexible vs rigid flat feet, shoe selection, and expert orthotic solutions by Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
flat-feet.intro: Flat feet is a common condition where the arch on the inside of the foot is flattened, allowing the entire sole of the foot to touch the floor when standing. Most infants and toddlers have flat feet because the arch hasn't formed yet and is hidden by baby fat. The arch typically develops throughout childhood up to age 8 to 10.
symptoms: Absence of a visible arch when the child stands up.
Foot, ankle, or calf pain, especially after physical activity.
Shoes wearing out quickly on the inner side.
The child complains of tired legs or avoids running and playing active games.
causes: Flexible Flat Foot: The most common type, where an arch is visible when the child sits or stands on tip-toes, but disappears when standing flat. This is benign.
Rigid Flat Foot: A structural abnormality where the arch is absent in all positions, often caused by congenital bone fusions (tarsal coalition).
Tight Achilles tendon: Restricts the flexibility of the foot.
flat-feet.treatment: Flexible flat feet do not require treatment if they are pain-free. If causing discomfort, Dr. Ayesha Saeed prescribes custom orthotic shoe inserts, arch supports, and targeted stretching exercises for the calf muscles. For rigid flat feet caused by structural issues like tarsal coalitions, treatment ranges from casting and orthotics to surgical reconstruction in adolescents who experience severe pain.

rickets.name: Nutritional & Metabolic Rickets
rickets.seo_title: Rickets Treatment in Pakistan | Child Bone Deficiency Doctor
rickets.seo_description: Comprehensive screening and medical management of Rickets in children. Expert guidance on Vitamin D and calcium from Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
rickets.intro: Rickets is the softening and weakening of bones in children, usually due to an extreme and prolonged deficiency of Vitamin D, Calcium, or Phosphate. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus from the food. A deficiency makes it difficult to maintain proper calcium levels in bones, leading to skeletal deformities and growth delays.
symptoms: Delayed growth and physical developmental milestones.
Delayed eruption of teeth and weakened enamel.
Skeletal deformities including bow legs, knock knees, a projecting breastbone (pigeon chest), and thickened wrists and ankles.
Muscle weakness and bone pain in the spine, pelvis, and legs.
causes: Lack of Sunlight: The body produces Vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. Children in indoor environments are at risk.
Dietary Deficiency: Diets lacking Vitamin D and calcium (e.g., lack of dairy products or breastfed infants without Vitamin D supplementation).
Malabsorption: Celiac disease or inflammatory bowel disease impairing nutrient absorption.
rickets.treatment: Most cases of rickets can be treated with oral Vitamin D and calcium supplements under strict clinical monitoring. Dr. Ayesha Saeed designs personalized metabolic recovery plans for infants and children, adjusting dosages based on lab assessments. For children who have developed severe skeletal deformities (like severe bow legs) that do not resolve with medical therapy, corrective orthopedic surgery (guided growth or osteotomy) is implemented once the bones have strengthened.

scoliosis.name: Scoliosis (Spine Curvature)
scoliosis.seo_title: Scoliosis Treatment Pakistan | Pediatric Spine Specialist
scoliosis.seo_description: Advanced Scoliosis bracing and surgical treatment for infants, children, and teens in Karachi and Lahore. Led by Canada-trained Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
scoliosis.intro: Scoliosis is an abnormal sideways curvature of the spine, most commonly diagnosed during the growth spurt just before puberty. While most cases are mild, some spine curves continue to worsen as children grow, leading to physical deformity, back pain, and in severe cases, reduced lung space and breathing difficulties.
symptoms: Uneven shoulders where one shoulder blade appears more prominent.
An uneven waistline, or one hip sitting higher than the other.
One side of the rib cage jutting forward when bending over (rib hump).
The head is not centered directly over the pelvis.
causes: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: The most common form, with no clear single cause, but often running in families.
Congenital Scoliosis: Due to spine bones failing to form properly during embryonic development.
Neuromuscular Scoliosis: Associated with conditions like Cerebral Palsy or Muscular Dystrophy.
scoliosis.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed provides comprehensive scoliosis care. Mild curves (under 20 degrees) are managed with close monitoring and regular X-rays. Moderate curves in growing children are treated with custom-molded orthopedic braces to prevent the curve from progressing. Severe curves (typically over 45-50 degrees) require surgical correction using **spinal fusion** with growing rods or spinal instrumentation, restoring vertical alignment and protecting chest cavity growth.

growth-plate-injuries.name: Growth Plate Injuries
growth-plate-injuries.seo_title: Growth Plate Injury Doctor | Child Fracture Specialist Pakistan
growth-plate-injuries.seo_description: Growth plate injuries require urgent specialist care to prevent permanent limb deformities. Internationally trained care by Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
growth-plate-injuries.intro: The growth plate (physeal plate) is a specialized area of developing cartilage near the ends of long bones in children and adolescents. Because growth plates are the last portion of the bones to harden, they are highly vulnerable to fractures. An improperly treated growth plate injury can result in the bone growing crooked or stopping growth prematurely.
symptoms: Inability to put weight on the affected limb or move it.
Severe pain and tenderness, particularly when pressing on the growth plate area.
Visible swelling, warmth, and bruising around the joint.
Crookedness or deformity in the limb.
causes: Trauma: Falls from playground equipment, bicycles, or stairs.
Sports Injuries: High-impact contact sports or repetitive stress from training.
Pediatric Trauma: Car accidents or severe impact injuries.
growth-plate-injuries.treatment: Treating growth plate injuries requires precise anatomical restoration. Dr. Ayesha Saeed evaluates these injuries using advanced imaging. Simple, non-displaced fractures are managed conservatively with custom casts or splints (serial casting and close X-ray follow-up). Displaced fractures require manipulation (**closed reduction**) or surgery (**open reduction internal fixation**) using smooth pins or screws that bypass the growth plate to preserve normal growth potential.

pediatric-fractures.name: Pediatric Fractures & Casts
pediatric-fractures.seo_title: Pediatric Fracture Specialist Pakistan | Child Bone Fractures
pediatric-fractures.seo_description: Expert pediatric fracture care by Dr. Ayesha Saeed. Pediatric bones heal differently; trust an internationally trained pediatric orthopedic surgeon.
pediatric-fractures.intro: Children's bones are vastly different from adult bones. They are more flexible, have a thicker covering (periosteum), and heal much faster. Because of this, children often experience unique fracture types, such as 'greenstick' fractures (where the bone bends and cracks but doesn't break all the way through) and buckle fractures. Proper alignment is critical to ensure normal bone remodelling.
symptoms: Sudden, intense pain immediately following an injury or fall.
Swelling, bruising, and visible deformity at the injury site.
Inability to move or use the arm or leg.
Tenderness or localized pain when touched.
causes: Playground accidents: Falls from swings, slides, or monkey bars.
Sports trauma: Fractures resulting from contact or impact during athletic activities.
Accidental falls: Simple slips at home or outdoors.
pediatric-fractures.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed provides expert fracture management. Many childhood fractures can be treated without surgery through **closed reduction** (gently setting the bone under sedation) and applying a lightweight, child-friendly cast. Thanks to the child's active growth, minor misalignments often straighten out naturally (bone remodeling). If the fracture is unstable, open, or involves a joint, minimally invasive surgery with thin pins or flexible rods is used to ensure stability.

sports-injuries.name: Pediatric Sports Injuries
sports-injuries.seo_title: Pediatric Sports Injuries Doctor | Young Athlete Care Pakistan
sports-injuries.seo_description: Specialized diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in children and teens. Keep your young athlete safe and active with Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
sports-injuries.intro: As children become more active in organized sports, pediatric sports injuries are on the rise. Because children have open growth plates and developing ligaments, their injuries differ significantly from adult athletic injuries. Common issues include overuse syndromes, growth plate inflammation (like Osgood-Schlatter disease), ligament sprains, and joint dislocations.
symptoms: Persistent pain or swelling in a joint after sports practice or play.
Limping or stiffness in the morning or during activity.
Sudden pain accompanied by a 'popping' sound or locking joint.
Reduced range of motion or instability in the knee or shoulder.
causes: Overuse: Repetitive training without adequate rest or conditioning.
Acute Trauma: Sudden twists, collisions, or falls during competitive matches.
Improper Technique: Poor form, unsupportive footwear, or insufficient warm-up.
sports-injuries.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed focuses on keeping young athletes active while protecting their long-term bone development. Most pediatric sports injuries are managed conservatively with activity modification, physical therapy, bracing, and structured rehabilitation. For ligament tears (such as ACL injuries in teenagers) or joint instability, she performs specialized pediatric-specific surgeries designed to protect the growth plates.

walking-problems.name: Walking Abnormalities (Intoeing & Limping)
walking-problems.seo_title: Walking Abnormalities Specialist | Child Gait Evaluation Pakistan
walking-problems.seo_description: Is your child walking with turned-in toes, flat feet, or limping? Get a professional pediatric gait analysis by Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
walking-problems.intro: Walking abnormalities are common concerns for parents. They include intoeing (pigeon-toeing), outtoeing, toe-walking, and limping. While intoeing and outtoeing are usually normal developmental variations that correct themselves as the child grows, a sudden limp or severe walking deformity requires immediate medical evaluation to rule out hip infections or bone disorders.
symptoms: Toes pointing inward or outward instead of straight ahead while walking.
Walking on tip-toes past the age of 2 years.
Frequent tripping or stumbling.
A sudden or progressive limp, which may or may not be painful.
causes: Metatarsus Adductus: The front of the foot turns inward, often due to positioning in the womb.
Tibial Torsion: The shinbone is twisted inward.
Femoral Anteversion: The thighbone is rotated inward, commonly causing children to sit in a 'W' position.
Inflammatory or Infectious hip conditions (e.g., transient synovitis).
walking-problems.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed conducts computerized and clinical gait assessments. Developmental intoeing and outtoeing almost always resolve without treatment by age 8 to 10. Braces and orthopedic shoes are rarely necessary. For persistent toe-walking, physical therapy and stretching are recommended. A sudden painful limp is investigated immediately with blood tests and imaging to identify and treat conditions like hip infections or slips.

hip-disorders.name: Pediatric Hip Disorders
hip-disorders.seo_title: Pediatric Hip Specialist | Dr. Ayesha Saeed Karachi & Lahore
hip-disorders.seo_description: Expert diagnosis and advanced care for pediatric hip conditions, including Perthes Disease, SCFE, and Transient Synovitis.
hip-disorders.intro: Skeletally immature hips are prone to a unique set of disorders. These include Perthes Disease (temporary loss of blood supply to the hip joint ball), Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE - the growth plate at the hip joint slips), and Transient Synovitis (irritable hip). Prompt diagnosis is essential to preserve the shape and function of the hip joint.
symptoms: Pain in the hip, groin, thigh, or knee (knee pain can often be referred hip pain).
Limping or stiffness in the hip joint.
Inability to rotate the leg inward or lift the leg.
Fever and refusal to bear weight (signs of septic arthritis, a medical emergency).
causes: Avascular necrosis: Disrupted blood flow to the femoral head (Perthes).
Growth plate weakness: Shearing forces causing the hip joint ball to slip (SCFE), common in adolescents.
Inflammatory response: Irritable hip following a viral upper respiratory tract infection.
hip-disorders.treatment: Treatment varies by condition. Irritable hip is managed with rest and anti-inflammatory medications. Perthes disease focuses on keeping the femoral head inside the socket using bracing or pelvic osteotomy surgery. SCFE requires surgical stabilization with a single screw to prevent further slippage. Septic arthritis requires immediate surgical joint washout to protect the cartilage.

bone-deformities.name: Limb & Bone Deformities
bone-deformities.seo_title: Limb Deformity Correction Pakistan | Pediatric Orthopedics
bone-deformities.seo_description: Advanced correction of congenital and acquired limb length discrepancies and deformities in Pakistan. Trained at SickKids Toronto.
bone-deformities.intro: Limb deformities can be congenital (present at birth) or acquired (resulting from fractures, growth plate damage, or bone infections). They include limb length discrepancies (one leg shorter than the other) and angular deformities of the arms or legs. These conditions can impact posture, walking, and lead to early joint deterioration.
symptoms: Visible difference in the length of the arms or legs.
Angular deformity (crooked arm or leg bone).
Limping, pelvic tilt, or walking on tip-toes on the shorter leg.
Decreased function or range of motion in the affected limb.
causes: Congenital disorders: Conditions like fibular hemimelia or hemihypertrophy.
Physeal arrest: Growth plate damage from a previous fracture or infection.
Metabolic bone diseases: Severe untreated rickets causing bone bending.
bone-deformities.treatment: Dr. Ayesha Saeed employs advanced deformity correction techniques. Mild limb differences are managed with shoe lifts. Angular deformities and significant length discrepancies are treated using **Guided Growth** in younger children, or surgical osteotomy (cutting the bone) and applying **internal fixators (magnetic lengthening rods)** or external frames (Ilizarov) to slowly straighten and lengthen the limb.

joint-pain.name: Bone & Joint Pain in Children
joint-pain.seo_title: Child Joint Pain Specialist Pakistan | Dr. Ayesha Saeed
joint-pain.seo_description: Is your child complaining of bone or joint pain? Differentiate growing pains from serious conditions with expert pediatric orthopedic care.
joint-pain.intro: While children often experience minor bumps and bruises, persistent bone or joint pain is not normal. Differentiating between benign 'growing pains' (which typically occur in the evening in both legs and have no swelling) and serious issues like juvenile arthritis, bone infections, or tumors is essential for early diagnosis and treatment.
symptoms: Persistent pain, swelling, warmth, or redness in a joint.
Pain accompanied by fever, fatigue, or unexplained weight loss.
Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes.
Pain that wakes the child from sleep or prevents weight-bearing.
causes: Growing Pains: Harmless muscle pain occurring in young children during growth spurts, usually at night.
Infections: Osteomyelitis (bone infection) or Septic Arthritis (joint infection).
Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: Chronic joint inflammation.
Trauma or Overuse: Micro-tears in ligaments or tendons from sports.
joint-pain.treatment: Growing pains are managed with reassurance, massage, warm baths, and mild pain relievers. Inflammatory or infectious joint pain requires immediate medical intervention, including intravenous antibiotics for infections, joint drainage if necessary, or rheumatology referrals for arthritis. Dr. Ayesha Saeed provides thorough assessments to identify the precise cause of pain.

congenital-bone-conditions.name: Congenital Bone & Joint Disorders
congenital-bone-conditions.seo_title: Congenital Bone Disorders Pakistan | Expert Pediatric Orthopedics
congenital-bone-conditions.seo_description: Specialized orthopedic care for children born with congenital bone conditions. Internationally trained treatment by Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
congenital-bone-conditions.intro: Congenital bone and joint disorders are skeletal abnormalities present at birth. They range from simple extra digits (polydactyly) to complex conditions like Osteogenesis Imperfecta (brittle bone disease), arthrogryposis, and skeletal dysplasias (dwarfism). These conditions require comprehensive, long-term multidisciplinary management.
symptoms: Missing or extra fingers or toes.
Severe stiffness or webbing in joints at birth.
Bones that fracture very easily with minimal or no trauma.
Proportionate or disproportionate short stature.
causes: Genetic Mutations: Alterations in DNA that impact bone and collagen formation.
Environmental/Intrauterine factors: Restricted fetal space or maternal drug exposure.
Spontaneous gene changes: New genetic variations not inherited from parents.
congenital-bone-conditions.treatment: Treatment is customized for each child. For brittle bone disease, Dr. Ayesha Saeed utilizes medical therapy (bisphosphonates) to strengthen bones, combined with **telescoping rod surgery (Fassier-Duval rods)** that expand as the child grows to prevent fractures. Simple deformities like extra digits are corrected with minor aesthetic surgeries in infancy. Rigid joints are managed with early casting and therapy.

posture-problems.name: Posture Problems in Children
posture-problems.seo_title: Child Posture Specialist Pakistan | Poor Posture Correction
posture-problems.seo_description: Is your child slouching? Learn about the impact of screen time on spine health and explore postural correction programs by Dr. Ayesha Saeed.
posture-problems.intro: Postural problems in children are becoming increasingly common due to sedentary lifestyles, heavy school bags, and prolonged screen time. Issues include slouching (postural kyphosis), rounded shoulders, and head tilt. While most cases are due to poor habits, some structural spine problems like Scheuermann's Kyphosis require medical intervention.
symptoms: Persistent rounding of the upper back (slouching).
Shoulders slouched forward and head jutting forward.
Back pain or muscle fatigue after sitting at a desk or using devices.
Inability to stand completely straight when asked.
causes: Poor ergonomic habits: Slouching while reading, writing, or using mobile phones.
Weak core muscles: Insufficient physical activity to support the spine.
Scheuermann's Disease: A structural condition where the spine vertebrae grow wedge-shaped.
Heavy backpacks: Carrying loads exceeding 10-15% of the child's body weight.
posture-problems.treatment: Postural kyphosis is treated non-surgically through postural training, core strengthening exercises, ergonomic desk setups, and limiting screen time. Dr. Ayesha Saeed advises parents on school backpack safety and correct sitting styles. Structural kyphosis is managed with physical therapy, custom back braces, or in very rare, severe progressive cases, surgical spine fusion.
